findings.detail: contract.md says invalid owner/key/text types or empty strings return400. handle validates body.key and body.text but never validates trusted_owner before passing it to SQLite. findings.title: Identical concurrent creates are incorrectly documented as possibly409

findings.detail: The sole test attempt returned SOURCE_POLICY. Nested import sqlite3 is outside the frozen source subset, separately from the excluded IntegrityError attribute. Semantic/manual claims about concurrency are not observed test evidence.

findings.detail: The task requires malformed resources to return403 and README defines resource as {owner,data}. Source returns200 with data=None for {trusted_owner:"a",resource:{owner:"a"}}, because data presence is never checked. The adversarial threat model explicitly promises both required keys and denial of this exact malformed shape. Frozen tests omit it; their numeric PASS is preserved but independent output approval is withheld.
findings.title: Malformed resource without data is authorized

findings.detail: The implementation accepts truthy non-string identity values and compares them with Python equality; 1 and True compare equal. An exact typed-identity claim needs an explicit identifier-type contract and tests. This is recorded as a limit, independently of the blocking missing-data defect.
findings.title: Identifier-type semantics are not established

import json,tempfile,pathlib
from api import handle
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
 results=[]
 for index,owner in enumerate(['',None]):
  db=str(pathlib.Path(d)/(str(index)+'.db'))
  results.append({'owner':owner,'result':handle(owner,{'key':'review-key','text':'one'},db)})
 print(json.dumps(results))
